page.text:
Now that we have described the abstract concept of a set, and have
defined a concrete set, we can express one of the axioms of
Zermelo-Frankel set theory that enables that set to exist.

```mlg
[\axiom.of.empty.set]
Axiom:
then:
. exists: E is \set
  suchThat: E = \empty.set
Id: "f2180719-568d-4084-982b-a71c5f195bf6"
```

With that, we can update our definition of a `\set` to indicate that a
set must satisfy the axiom of empty sets.

```mlg
[\set]
Describes: X
satisfies:
. \axiom.of.empty.set
Requires:
. capability: x_ "in" X :-> \\abstract
Documented:
. called: "set"
Id: "a0759217-e1f6-412c-982a-0038cd17a3a1"
```

Now this definition of a set is incomplete because there are many more
axioms in Zermelo-Frankel set theory, but this document isn't meant to be
exhaustive but instead give an introduction to describing concepts in
Mathlingua. As such, we won't add the other axioms to focus on more
aspects of Mathlingua.
